title: Backward Direction via Inner Product Expansion
content: Proves that if $u = c \cdot v$ then $\|\langle u, v\rangle\| = \|u\| \cdot \|v\|$. The proof rewrites $\langle c \cdot v, v\rangle = \bar{c} \cdot \langle v, v\rangle = \bar{c} \cdot \|v\|^2$ using `inner_smul_left` and `inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K`. Then $\|\bar{c} \cdot \|v\|^2\| = \|c\| \cdot \|v\|^2 = \|c \cdot v\| \cdot \|v\|$. The `starRingEnd_apply` and `norm_star` handle the conjugation ($\|\bar{c}\| = \|c\|$), and `ring` closes the algebraic identity.

title: Orthogonal Projection Residual Lemma
content: The heart of the proof: the residual $u - \frac{\langle v, u\rangle}{\langle v, v\rangle} v$ is orthogonal to $v$. This is the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization step for a single vector. The proof uses `inner_sub_left` (linearity in the first argument), `inner_smul_left` (pulling out the scalar with conjugation), `inner_conj_symm` ($\overline{\langle x,y\rangle} = \langle y,x\rangle$), then `field_simp` and `ring` to cancel. The hypothesis $v \neq 0$ ensures $\langle v,v\rangle \neq 0$ for the division.
mathContext: $\left\langle u - \frac{\langle v, u\rangle}{\langle v, v\rangle} v,\, v \right\rangle = \langle u, v\rangle - \frac{\overline{\langle v, u\rangle}}{\overline{\langle v, v\rangle}} \langle v, v\rangle = \langle u, v\rangle - \langle u, v\rangle = 0$

title: Forward Direction: Projection Coefficient Setup
content: Sets $c = \langle v, u\rangle / \langle v, v\rangle$ and establishes the orthogonality of the residual $w = u - cv$ to $v$. The `set` tactic introduces $c$ as a local definition with its defining equation available as `hc_def`. This is the standard orthogonal projection in inner product spaces — the coefficient $c$ is chosen precisely so the residual is perpendicular to $v$.
mathContext: $c = \frac{\langle v, u\rangle_\mathbb{K}}{\langle v, v\rangle_\mathbb{K}} = \frac{\langle v, u\rangle}{\|v\|^2}$

title: Pythagorean Theorem Application
content: Since $u - cv \perp cv$, the Pythagorean theorem gives $\|u\|^2 = \|u - cv\|^2 + \|cv\|^2$. The proof splits $u = (u - cv) + cv$ via `abel`, then applies `norm_add_sq` (the parallelogram-like identity $\|a+b\|^2 = \|a\|^2 + 2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle + \|b\|^2$) with the cross term vanishing due to orthogonality. This decomposition is the key geometric idea: it expresses $\|u\|^2$ as the sum of the projection length and the residual length.

title: Computing ‖⟪u,v⟫‖ from the Decomposition
content: Shows $\|\langle u, v\rangle\| = \|c\| \cdot \|v\|^2$. Since $\langle u - cv, v\rangle = 0$, we have $\langle u, v\rangle = \langle cv, v\rangle = \bar{c} \cdot \|v\|^2$. Taking norms: $\|\langle u,v\rangle\| = \|c\| \cdot \|v\|^2$. The proof uses the same split $u = (u-cv) + cv$, then `inner_add_left` with the orthogonality to eliminate the residual term.

title: Equality Forces Residual to Vanish
content: The crucial step: from the hypothesis $\|\langle u,v\rangle\| = \|u\| \cdot \|v\|$ and the computation $\|\langle u,v\rangle\| = \|c\| \cdot \|v\|^2$, we derive $\|c\| \cdot \|v\| = \|u\|$ (canceling one $\|v\|$ factor). Then Pythagoras gives $\|u - cv\|^2 = \|u\|^2 - \|cv\|^2 = 0$. The algebraic heart is the cancellation step using `mul_right_cancel₀` (division by $\|v\| \neq 0$), followed by `pow_eq_zero_iff` to extract $\|u-cv\| = 0$ from $\|u-cv\|^2 = 0$.

title: Main Theorem: Complex CS Equality Characterization
content: The headline result: for $v \neq 0$ in a complex inner product space, $\|\langle u, v\rangle_\mathbb{C}\| = \|u\| \cdot \|v\|$ if and only if $u = cv$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$. This answers the open question from `cauchy-schwarz-oq-01`: the real equality characterization extends to complex spaces with the natural generalization that the proportionality constant can be complex. The `constructor` tactic splits the iff, using the forward and backward results.
mathContext: $\|\langle u, v\rangle_\mathbb{C}\| = \|u\| \cdot \|v\| \iff \exists c \in \mathbb{C}: u = c \cdot v$

title: Uniform RCLike Version
content: Generalizes the result to any `RCLike` field $\mathbb{K}$ (Lean's typeclass for fields isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$). The proof is identical to the complex version — the key insight is that the entire argument uses only sesquilinearity, positive definiteness, and conjugate symmetry, which are axioms of `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E` for any `RCLike 𝕜`. This demonstrates the power of Lean's typeclass system: one proof covers infinitely many concrete instantiations.

title: Edge Cases: Zero Vectors
content: When either vector is zero, both sides of the CS inequality equal zero, so equality holds trivially. These are proved by `simp` with the inner product's linearity in each argument (`inner_zero_right`, `inner_zero_left`). These edge cases complete the characterization: the main iff theorem requires $v \neq 0$, but these lemmas cover the remaining case.

title: Symmetric Version via Conjugate Symmetry
content: Proves the symmetric form: $\|\langle u, v\rangle\| = \|u\|\|v\| \iff \exists c, v = cu$ (for $u \neq 0$). The key step uses $\|\langle u, v\rangle\| = \|\overline{\langle u, v\rangle}\| = \|\langle v, u\rangle\|$ via `inner_conj_symm` and the fact that conjugation preserves norm. Then `mul_comm` swaps $\|u\|\|v\|$ to $\|v\|\|u\|$, reducing to the original characterization with roles exchanged.
mathContext: $\|\langle u, v\rangle\| = \|\overline{\langle u, v\rangle}\| = \|\langle v, u\rangle\|$, so swap $u \leftrightarrow v$

title: Summary: Both ℂ and RCLike Versions
content: Packages the complex-specific and uniform RCLike results into a single conjunction, serving as a formal summary. The conjunction of universally quantified statements witnesses that the open question is fully resolved: CS equality characterization works for all scalar fields satisfying the `RCLike` interface. The proof is a direct pair of the two main theorems.
mathContext: $(\forall_{\mathbb{C}\text{-IPS}}\, \text{CS-eq iff lin. dep.}) \wedge (\forall_{\mathbb{K}\text{-IPS}}\, \text{CS-eq iff lin. dep.})$
